t: For more than three thousand years the Egyptians worshipped many gods, among them Ra, Osiris, Isis, Horus, Amun, Ptah and Thoth, whose cult, carried out by the pharaoh and the temples, upheld maat, the order of the world, against chaos.

Its hope of eternal life inspired the pyramids, mummification, richly furnished tombs and the spells of the Book of the Dead, in which the heart of the dead was weighed before Osiris against the feather of maat.
Briefly overturned by Akhenaten’s worship of the sun disc, it endured through Persian, Greek and Roman rule, carried the cult of Isis across the Roman Empire, and faded with the rise of Christianity.
dyk: The catacombs dedicated to the jackal god Anubis at Saqqara held some eight million mummified animals, most of them dogs, offered by pilgrims to the god.
ev: Egypt is united under the first kings, who rule as the god Horus on earth
The Great Pyramid is built at Giza as the tomb of the king Khufu
The Pyramid Texts, Egypt’s oldest religious writings, are carved in the pyramid of Unas
Akhenaten raises the Aten, the sun disc, above all other gods and founds a new capital at Amarna
Rome annexes Egypt; its emperors are portrayed on temple walls as pharaohs
The Serapeum of Alexandria is destroyed after the emperor Theodosius bans pagan sacrifice
The last known hieroglyphic inscription is carved at the temple of Philae
Officials of the emperor Justinian close the temple of Isis at Philae

f.origin: The Nile valley, with prehistoric roots; shaped with the first kings around 3100 BCE
f.founder: None: it grew from the cults of Egypt’s towns and kings; the pharaoh Akhenaten briefly imposed the worship of the Aten in the 14th century BCE
f.scriptures: No single scripture: the Pyramid Texts, Coffin Texts and Book of the Dead for the afterlife, with hymns, myths and temple inscriptions
f.followers: None as a living tradition: the last temple, of Isis at Philae, closed around 537; small modern revivals draw on it
